# Instructions for accurately documenting failed advertised specifications in a consumer product performance report

1. Start with the test records.

completion:
Capture all the product specifications as advertised by the manufacturer. These specifications should be directly compared to the actual performance results from the product testing. This comparison gives a clear idea of the parameters in which the product has failed to meet the advertised specifications.

3. Organize the data.
Collect and organize all the data obtained from individual tests into a coherent format. Ensure that every piece of data is clearly documented, and each test result corresponds with the intended specification.

4. Detail the test environment and conditions.
Describe the testing environment, including relevant conditions (such as temperature, humidity, pressure, etc.) that might have had an effect on the performance outcomes. This step helps provide context to explain any failures considering the intended operational environment.

5. Document the test methodology.
Provide information on the standard test methodologies used to evaluate the product performance. This will help in corroborating the legitimacy and accuracy of testing procedures and results.
